nora (People Ops): Heads up team // Diego's consular appointment in Mexico got pushed out by 6 weeks due to limited slots. This could affect his travel and start date.

diego (Newhire): Oh no. I was planning to start from the Mexico office May 2. Can I start remotely from there until stamping is done?

emma (Hiring Manager): We need Diego on-site for the week of May 9 for onboarding workshops with the infra team. Any remote workaround?

rita (Immigration Counsel): Quick summary: If Diego is a foreign national needing consular stamping, he can't re-enter US on H-1B without the new stamp. Options: (1) delay US entry/start, (2) start as remote offshore employee until stamping completes, or (3) onboard as a contractor interim (with tax implications). We can't have him perform US-prohibited work from Mexico if the contract is US-only; check client/location clauses.

payroll-bot: Note: Remote offshore hire vs contractor affects payroll country setup. Offshore payroll for Mexico requires local payroll vendor; that takes ~5 business days to stand up. Contractor option requires W-9 (not applicable) or equivalent local vendor docs.

travel-coordinator: Embassy backlog varies by consulate. Some candidates secure an expedited slot with a letter; others move to a different consulate with availability. Diego, do you have flexibility on consulate city?

diego (Newhire): I can travel to Guadalajara or Mexico City, but flights add cost. I can start remote from Mexico if legally allowed. Prefer not to delay start.

emma (Hiring Manager): We could push the intensive in-person week to June if needed, but that slows the feature timeline. Is hybrid possible? Diego shadows remotely and joins week of 6/6 in person?

rita (Immigration Counsel): Hybrid could work. From compliance standpoint: (a) remote work from Mexico is allowed if local employment laws are followed and benefits aligned, (b) if we treat as US hire working abroad temporarily, we need a signed secondment addendum and tax signoff. I'll draft a short secondment template.

payroll-bot: For tax and benefits: if Diego remains on US payroll while working from Mexico >30 days, we need tax team review and possibly local payroll. Recommend contractor/local payroll for the interim to avoid permanent establishment risk. Finance will sign off.

onboard-bot: Reminder: benefits enrollment window opens on first US payroll run. If Diego is on local payroll or contractor, benefits enrollment may need manual intervention.

nora (People Ops): Proposed plan: 1) Put Diego on a 6-week offshore contractor agreement (local vendor or 1099-equivalent) to allow immediate start remote. 2) Travel team to hunt expedited consulate slots and alternate cities. 3) Immigration (Rita) to draft secondment/transition language for conversion back to W-2 post-stamp. 4) Finance to confirm pay parity for the interim.

emma (Hiring Manager): OK with that if pay parity and guaranteed conversion date. We need Diego in-person for the June week.

diego (Newhire): Fine with contractor for 6 weeks if payroll is comparable. Please send the agreement. I'm happy to travel for an earlier slot if company covers flight.

rita (Immigration Counsel): I'll prepare two docs: (A) short contractor onboarding clause for interim remote work, (B) conversion addendum to sign once Diego returns/stamps. Also will draft a consulate letter template requesting expedited appointment (we use a limited criteria but can try).

payroll-bot: Finance note: to mirror base salary as contractor for first 30 days we need vendor packet + local tax form. If company pays flights, submit expense approval to expenses queue.

travel-coordinator: I'll scrape consulate availability across MX consulates and set up an alert. Diego, DM me passport number and preferred dates. I'll prioritize Mexico City and Guadalajara.

nora (People Ops): Action items and owners (TL;DR):
``
- Rita: Draft contractor + conversion addenda and consulate letter template (due EOD tomorrow)
- Payroll/Finance: Confirm interim pay parity & vendor path (by 24 hrs)
- Travel: Search expedited slots + alternate consulates, confirm coverage for travel cost (by 48 hrs)
- Diego: DM passport + availability, sign interim contractor when ready
- Emma: Confirm in-person week of 6/6 is flexible if needed
```

emma (Hiring Manager): I'll block June 6-10 on calendars tentatively and adjust if stamping clears earlier.

diego (Newhire): Sent passport via DM. Thanks all 60a

nora (People Ops): Thanks team. We'll aim to keep the start date May 2 remote and convert to W-2 after stamping. I'll post updates here. :rocket:
